technique.summary: Exploit time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) gaps by sending multiple concurrent requests. This can lead to double-spending, multi-use of single-use tokens, bypassing rate limits, or corrupting application state.
steps: Identify operations that should be atomic: balance transfers, coupon redemption, vote submission
Prepare the request that performs the sensitive operation
Use HTTP/2 single-packet attack or connection warming to synchronize concurrent requests
Send 10-20 concurrent identical requests in a single TCP packet (last-byte sync)
Check if the operation was executed multiple times (balance deducted once but credited multiple times)
Vary the number of concurrent requests and timing to find the race window

bypassTechniques: HTTP/2 single-packet attack: send all requests in one TCP packet for maximum synchronization
Connection warming: pre-establish connections, then send requests simultaneously
Vary request count and timing — some race windows are wider than others
Try from multiple source IPs if server uses per-IP queuing
